title: Emberline Manufacturing — Offline Inference Scaling & Cutover Plan
content:
Purpose
This is a working proposal for Emberline Manufacturing's private inference deployment (air-gapped site in Phoenix DC). Focus: offline inference fleet sizing for batch/nearline workloads, Terraform module mapping, and an executable cutover + rollback checklist. Treat as engineering-first notes — still waiting on final network ACLs and rack-level power confirmation from customer facilities.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Target workload: nightly/shifted batch runs + sporadic nearline queries (99% throughput sensitivity, 95th pct latency not critical).
- Recommended hardware: mixed H100-80GB and A10G nodes for cost/perf balance.
- Deployment shape: 6 worker racks (4 H100 nodes per rack) + 8 A10G nodes for smaller model variants and preprocessing. Controller/serving plane run on 3 control VMs in separate network segment with HA.
- Terraform approach: reuse terraform-modules/inference-cluster (PR#614) with new variables: emberline_region_id, rack_id_map, customer_kms_key_arn.

Assumptions (call these out)
- Customer will provide 10Gb uplink per rack and BGP peering to our control-plane VPN. If only 1Gb available, throughput drops ~7–10x; need to flag.
- Typical batch job: 512 sequences x 2k tokens on average; concurrency target 8 jobs in parallel during peak 2-hour window.
- Model family: two families — open-weights-7B (quantized int4) and open-weights-70B (FP16 / 8-bit quant experiments). Expect ~60% of tokens on 7B requests.
- CA cert + SSO will be handled by customer (we will consume SAML metadata).

Sizing rationale (back-of-envelope)
- H100-80GB: prefer for 70B loads. One H100 can sustain ~9000 tokens/s for short seqs (<=1024) FP16; for our 2k median seq, estimate 3.5–4k tokens/s. With 6 racks x 4 nodes = 24 H100s => ~96k tokens/s nominal across 70B capacity (but real effective lower due to KV/cache warmups and batching inefficiencies).
- A10G: workhorse for 7B quantized int4. One A10G node (with 48GB host RAM) supports ~18k tokens/s for these models. Eight nodes => ~144k tokens/s reserved for 7B traffic.
- Headroom: keep 25–30% spare capacity for rollouts and canary traffic. Target reserved capacity: 18 H100 + 12 A10G active, rest as standby for maintenance.
- Storage: model artifacts + cache volume per H100 node: 750GB NVMe local (hot), plus NFS for checkpoints (2TB).

Network & security notes
- VPC design: three subnets — control-plane (private, NAT egress), worker-plane (private, no internet), mgmt-plane (bastion + jump hosts with restricted access).
- Peering: site <-> Redwood control plane via IPsec site-to-site; BGP advertised prefixes for worker ranges. Recommend explicit route filters to block ephemeral public ranges.
- KMS/HSM: customer to provide CMK; Terraform will store key ARN in ssm param and mount to controllers. No keys will leave customer network.
- TLS: mutual TLS for runtime RPC; fingerprints pinned in agent config.

Terraform module notes (implementation guidance and TODOs)
- Modules to reuse: inference-cluster (v2.1), vpc-peering (v1.4), kms-connector (v0.9). Changes needed: 
  - inference-cluster: expose `gpu_type_list` as string list, add `rack_topology` var to map physical racks to availability sets.
  - vpc-peering: add optional `bgp_asn` and `prefix_filters` inputs (customer requires ASN 65101).
  - kms-connector: add `key_rotation_days` and `hsm_pkcs11_endpoint` optional inputs.
- State management: remote S3 backend + dynamodb lock not possible (air-gapped). We will use local-encrypted state stored on a jump-host (sftp to customer vault). Document transfer procedure in runbook.
- Secrets: use sealed-secrets pattern — TF only writes placeholders; at apply time a manual credential injection step (Ansible) will push private certs.
- Outputs: controllers_fqdn, worker_node_ids, ssh_bastion_ip. Add `tf_output_release_tag` to trace deploy revision.

Upgrade and cutover plan (phased)
Phase 0 — Preparation (weeks 0–2):
- Confirm rack power + PDU mapping; request labeled U positions.
- Validate customer firewall rules and agree on CIDRs.
- Converge on KMS key ARN and SAML metadata.
- Create ephemeral state storage host and rotate creds (OPS-REQ-112).

Phase 1 — Staging deploy (week 3):
- Deploy TF to staging racks (2 H100 + 2 A10G) using local state host.
- Run synthetic batch jobs (same payload shape) — measure tokens/s and tail latencies.
- Adjust batching configs in runtime (batch_window_ms, max_batch_tokens).

Phase 2 — Canary (week 4):
- Add 4 H100 + 4 A10G to canary pool. Route 5% of daily jobs to canary.
- Monitor: error rate, queue depth, GPU utilization, mem pressure. If error rate >0.5% sustained for 10m -> rollback.

Phase 3 — Full cutover (week 5):
- Gradually expand to target active set over 24–48h.
- Run two full-night runs; compare cost and perf vs baseline.

Rollback strategy
- If canary fails, stop routing new jobs to canary and drain. If controller-level regression discovered, fallback to hosted-compatible model variant via smart routing (requires peering to fallback endpoint; must be enabled in config ahead of cutover).
- Hardware failure: maintain spare nodes in on-site reserve; replacement flows documented in runbook with serial numbers and PXE images.

Operational runbook highlights (actionable commands)
- To drain a worker: `redwoodctl node drain --id <node-id> --timeout 1800s` (note: requires bastion-forwarding).
- To snapshot TF state to vault: `sftp deploy@vault:/states/emberline/$(date +%F)-state.tfstate.gpg` (GPG sign with ops key).
- To rotate KMS: `terraform apply -var 'customer_kms_key_arn=arn:aws:kms:...' -auto-approve` followed by `redwoodctl config reload`.

Monitoring & SLOs
- Placeholders for dashboards: GPU utilization per rack, model-level token/s, request queue latency (p50/p95/p99), cache hit ratio, and model degradation score (quality metric from eval harness).
- SLO example: maintain batch job completion within SLA window 99.5% per day. Alert on backlog growth >20% sustained over 15m.

Open questions for customer (needs answers before finalizing)
- Confirm physical rack U positions and the available PDUs (per-rack breakers).
- Will Emberline allow us to host a small outbound tunnel to Redwood control plane for telemetry? If no, we need to ship the collector appliance.
- Which CIDR to use for worker-plane? We proposed 10.240.0.0/18 but can change.
- Do they require FIPS 140-2 HSM for KMS keys? If yes, integration path changes and lead time increases.

Risks & mitigations
- Network bottleneck risk (10Gb not provisioned): mitigate by re-provisioning smaller batch sizes, add more local batching to increase utilization but higher latency for individual requests.
- State drift due to local encrypted state: mitigated by nightly GPG-signed snapshots and cross-check script.
- Quantization regression on 70B: recommend we ship a validation test harness to customer to run on a staging set before enabling int8/4.

Cost estimate (very rough)
- Hardware CAPEX (procurement): ~24 H100 @ list / negotiated pricing, 12 A10G, controllers and networking -> ballpark $2.1M–2.6M depending on vendor discounts.
- Operational cost: onsite support + spare parts: ~$42k/year.

Next steps (owner + date)
- Facilities confirmation (Ava) -> due 2026-03-05
- Finalize TF changes and open PR for rack_topology var (Diego) -> PR by 2026-02-28 (linked PR above)
- Customer call to decide KMS (Priya + Emberline Sec) -> schedule week of 2026-03-01

Notes to self / loose ends
- Need to add sample ansible playbook to push certs to controllers (stubbed in /ops/ansible/emberline).
- Add runbook snippet for air-gapped telemetry collector deployment (docker vs systemd).
- Check licensing terms for vendor model binaries when run fully on-prem.

End of draft — feedback welcome.
